paragraph: Angola's identity card rests on Law 4/09 on civil identification. The National Assembly amended it [in August 2017](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2017/lei-n-o-20-17-de-31-de-agosto/>) and [in January 2021](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2021/lei-n-o-3-21-de-25-de-janeiro/>). Under the law as amended, each card's [number acts in law as the unique citizen number](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2021/lei-n-o-3-21-de-25-de-janeiro/>). In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers [reviewed a civil and criminal identification bill](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/estado-angolano-encaixa-receitas-de-9-36-bilioes-de-kwanzas-para-oge-2026/>), and on 30 October [the Assembly approved two of its chapters in detail](<https://parlamento.ao/Noticia_72422>). No regulation or decree applying the law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need a regulation or decree applying the law, made in that time.

Burundi's identity card runs on ministerial ordinances of 1978 and 1986, which the government's procedures page, held as published in January 2026, [lists as its main texts](<https://isoko.gov.bi/?procedures=fichier-national-de-lidentification-carte-nationale-didentite>). The page names no identity law. It says further texts remain to be adopted before the national identification file is instituted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a law, ordinance or decree-law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card, however old.

Benin's law no. 2017-08 of 19 June 2017 on the identification of natural persons is the law behind the national register and the personal identification number. In June 2025 the National Assembly [adopted law no. 2025-12 amending its article 6](<https://www.lanation.bj/actualites/assemblee-nationale-larticle-6-de-la-loi-sur-lidentification-des-personnes-physiques-retouche>). Article 6 as amended [provides for a national biometric population register and a personal identification number](<https://www.lanation.bj/actualites/assemblee-nationale-larticle-6-de-la-loi-sur-lidentification-des-personnes-physiques-retouche>). In July 2025 the Council of Ministers [adopted a decree setting assurance levels for electronic identification schemes](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/cm/2025-07-02/>), made under the digital code. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a regulation or decree applying the identification law, made in the past three years.

On 11 October 2024 the transitional legislative assembly [adopted the bill on unique electronic identification of the natural person](<https://burkina24.com/2024/10/11/burkina-faso-la-loi-portant-identification-unique-et-electronique-de-la-personne-physique-adoptee/>). On 19 August 2025 the minister for digital transition [said the law had been adopted the previous year](<https://www.sidwaya.info/identification-electronique-des-personnes-le-programme-wuri-sensibilise-a-bobo-dioulasso/>). In the last twelve months, Africa24 TV [reported on 22 November 2026](<https://africa24tv.com/burkina-faso-enrolement-biometrique-de-masse-2-400-agents-deployes-sur-pres-de-12-000-sites/>) that the national enrolment under way since 11 November is framed by the 2024 law. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found. Mature would need a rule made under the law in the past three years, such as a regulation or decree applying it.

Botswana's National Registration Act [commenced on 31 December 1986](<https://botswanalaws.com/consolidated-statutes/principle-legislation/national-registration>). [The National Registration (Amendment) Act 2025 was assented on 23 March 2025](<https://www.botswanalaws.com/PDF/StatutesActpdf/2025Actpdf/007.pdf>), to start on a date the minister sets. Under it [the registrar assigns an identity number to each person in a Unified Population Register](<https://www.botswanalaws.com/PDF/StatutesActpdf/2025Actpdf/007.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the minister [said it now lets passports and driving licences serve as identification](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/90334>) while identity cards are replaced. No rule made under the Act since October 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the register.

Côte d'Ivoire's biometric identity project is [backed by the Law on Digital Identification, no. 2019-566](<https://www.ids.ac.uk/publications/biometric-digital-id-in-africa/>), an enacted law of five articles. A 2025 study of ten African identity systems treats it, an executive decree and the 2013 data protection law together as the legal basis of the system. The study says the 2019 law [establishes the legal basis for the biometric digital identity](<https://www.ids.ac.uk/publications/biometric-digital-id-in-africa/>) and describes the identity document as a secure card serving several applications. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years.

Cameroon's Law 2024/016, the new civil registration law, is [the law the national civil status office is implementing](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202510/cameroon-partners-with-liber-technologies-to-pursue-crvs-reforms>). This was reported in October 2025. The law [authorises digital birth, marriage and death certificates and a unique personal identification number for every citizen](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202510/cameroon-partners-with-liber-technologies-to-pursue-crvs-reforms>). It is an identity law as well as a civil registration law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found since September 2023. Mature would need a rule made under the law in the past three years, such as a regulation or decree applying it.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's population file was created by [the Prime Minister's decree no. 22/07 of 2 March 2022](<https://leganet.cd/Legislation/Droit%20Public/Identification/decret%2022.04.02.03.2022.html>), and no identity law is among its legal bases. In the last twelve months, on 12 June 2026 two deputies [tabled a private member's bill](<https://actualite.cd/2026/06/12/assemblee-nationale-venance-eyanga-et-patrick-namazihana-deposent-une-proposition-de-loi>) on the general rules for identifying natural persons. The bill is to go to committee. It had not been debated by the end of September 2026. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force.

The Republic of the Congo's unique identification number was [instituted by decree no. 2004-469 of 3 November 2004](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/relance-des-operations-de-production-de-la-carte-niu>), and no law is named behind it. The national identity card rests on a 2009 decree, which [decree no. 2024-2692 of 13 November 2024 amended](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/117585/COG-117585.pdf>). An order of 12 October 2022 [made the number mandatory](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/relance-des-operations-de-production-de-la-carte-niu>) for eight economic transactions and five administrative formalities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No identity law has been found, and no bill for one. Establishing would need a national identity law in force.

The Comoros has law no. 14-023/AU of 24 June 2014, [promulgated by decree no. 14-137/PR](<https://justice.gouv.km/texte/decret-n14-137-pr-portant-promulgation-de-la-loi-n14-023-au-instituant-la-carte-didentite-comorienne-numerique/>). The Ministry of Justice [describes the 2014 law as instituting the Comorian digital, biometric identity card](<https://justice.gouv.km/texte/decret-n14-137-pr-portant-promulgation-de-la-loi-n14-023-au-instituant-la-carte-didentite-comorienne-numerique/>). That title is what is held on the law's content. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need a rule made under the law in that time, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Cabo Verde's national civil identification and authentication system was [created by Law 43/VIII/2013 of 17 September 2013](<https://justica.gov.cv/sniac>). The national identification card was then [created by Decree-Law 19/2014 of 17 March](<https://sniac.cv/cartao-nacional-de-identificacao/>). The card is [an electronic one whose chip holds a digital certificate](<https://sniac.cv/cartao-nacional-de-identificacao/>). Two rules were made under the decree-law in 2017, one on biometric capture and one on the card's validity. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need a rule made under it in that time.

Djibouti's law no. 39/AN/19 on the identification of natural persons was [published on 21 January 2019](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n39-an-19-8eme-l-portant-identification-des-personnes-physiques-en-republique-de-djibouti-creation-du-numero-national-didentification-et-etablissement-dun-registre-national/>). It creates a unique national identification number and a national register. A decree of 13 July 2020 [was made under its article 9](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/decret-n2020-150-pr-mi-portant-composition-caracteristique-et-champ-dapplication-lies-au-numero-national-didentification-nni/>) and requires administrations, hospitals, schools, utilities and traders to carry the number on their documents. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

On 2 November 2025 Algeria's Council of Ministers [approved a draft law on trust services and digital identification](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0511-50150-algeria-updates-digital-services-and-online-identity-law>). In the last twelve months it became [law no. 26-02 of 17 February 2026](<https://www.mpt.gov.dz/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Loi-n%C2%B0-26-02.Services-de-Confiance.Identification-electronique.FR_.pdf>), which sets the rules for electronic identification. The Ministry of the Interior says [executive decree 10-210 of 16 September 2010 instituted the national identification number](<https://id4africa.com/2026/files/T2-3-S3-4-Algeria-FINAL.pdf>). No regulation or decree applying the 2026 law has been found. Mature would need a rule made under the law, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Ethiopia's Digital Identification Proclamation, no. 1284/2023, [passed the House of Peoples' Representatives in March 2023](<https://kanatelevision.com/news/what-is-faydaverse-the-ethiopian-national-id-program-that-became-a-company-and-how-it-plans-to/>). It was [signed by the President on 18 April 2023](<https://ethiodata.et/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Ethiopian-Digital-Identification-Proclamation-No.-1284_2023-1.pdf>). The proclamation [sets up a digital identification system that collects demographic and biometric data in a central database](<https://ethiodata.et/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Ethiopian-Digital-Identification-Proclamation-No.-1284_2023-1.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports a regulation or decree applying the law since September 2023. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years.

Ghana's identity system rests on two Acts that the National Identification Authority [lists as its laws](<https://nia.gov.gh/legal-and-regulations/>): the National Identification Authority Act, 2006 and the National Identity Register Act, 2008. In the last twelve months, regulations made under the 2008 Act were [gazetted on 27 March 2026 and in force from 9 June 2026](<https://www.mint.gov.gh/government-strengthens-identification-verification-system/>). They require organisations to verify identity through the Authority's system, [in real time against its database](<https://www.facebook.com/officialNIAGH/posts/press-releasegovernment-makes-biometric-verification-mandatory-for-ghana-card-ve/1522136326623174/>). Before them, [a notice of 15 February 2024](<https://nia.gov.gh/legal-and-regulations/>) had specified the portable card readers that may be used. The regulations came into force on 9 June 2026.

Guinea's Law L/2023/019/CNT of 25 October 2023 on the identification of physical persons [is the law under which a decree of April 2025 is made](<https://guineelex.com/decrets-arretes/decret-d-2025-052-prg-cnrd-sgg>). The decree [sets up a register of biographic and biometric data with a personal identification number](<https://guineelex.com/decrets-arretes/decret-d-2025-052-prg-cnrd-sgg>). In the last twelve months, on 26 February 2026 the head of the identification office [named the law at a workshop](<https://matd.gov.gn/loneci-vulgarise-les-nouvelles-lois-sur-letat-civil-et-de-lidentification/>). A January 2026 workshop at Kindia [reviewed and validated further draft decrees and orders](<https://ravec.gov.gn/ravec-kindia-atelier-de-relecture-et-validation-des-textes-dapplication-portant-etat-civil-et-identification-des-personnes-physiques/>) applying the identification and civil status laws. No source found says those drafts have been signed.

[Section 17 of the Nationality and Citizenship Act](<https://jollofnews.gm/barrows-call-for-16-year-olds-to-register-for-national-id-sparks-legal-questions/>) gives Gambian citizens aged 18 or over the right to a national identity card, Jollof News reported in June 2026. No separate national identity act has been found. The National Identification Authority runs the National Identity Management System. A [National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028](<https://www.uneca.org/stories/validation-of-the-gambia's-national-digital-id-and-digital-transformation-strategy>) was validated in 2024, and it is a strategy, not a law. In the last twelve months no source found says the law provides for a biometric register, a unique identity number or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

Kenya's National Integrated Identity Management System began under executive order no. 1 of 2018, and Kenya has [no stand-alone digital identity law](<https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/data-and-policy/article/an-assessment-of-the-legal-and-regulatory-framework-supporting-the-implementation-of-the-national-integrated-identity-management-system-niims-in-kenya/617BC651E2C09DE2CDD175C73A1C90E2>). The government then wrote the system into the 1947 Registration of Persons Act by an omnibus amendment. The High Court ruled in January 2020 that a comprehensive regulatory framework should be enacted before roll-out. The system is [anchored on the Huduma Namba regulations of 2020](<https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/data-and-policy/article/an-assessment-of-the-legal-and-regulatory-framework-supporting-the-implementation-of-the-national-integrated-identity-management-system-niims-in-kenya/617BC651E2C09DE2CDD175C73A1C90E2>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

Liberia's National Identification Registry Act was [approved by the President on 1 August 2011 and published on 8 August 2011](<https://citizenshiprightsafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Liberia-NIR-Act-2011.pdf>). It repeals a 1983 decree and sets up the National Identification Registry. The Act [sets up a National Biometric Identification System and a biometric card for each person](<https://citizenshiprightsafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Liberia-NIR-Act-2011.pdf>), enrolled with a fingerprint and a photograph. No later amendment is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Libya's Law No. 8 of 2014 on the National Number was [issued by the General National Congress on 24 March 2014](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-8-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2014%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A..pdf>) and took effect on issue. The law [provides for a twelve-digit national number unique to each citizen](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-8-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2014%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A..pdf>). It also provides for a national database completed with ten fingerprints, an iris print, a photograph and a signature. No amendment is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

Lesotho's National Identity Cards Act, 2011 was [published in the Government Gazette on 21 March 2011 and commenced on 1 July 2013](<https://lesotholii.org/akn/ls/act/2011/9/eng@2011-03-21>). The Act [establishes a National Identity Register that records fingerprints and an image](<https://lesotholii.org/akn/ls/act/2011/9/eng@2011-03-21>) for everyone aged sixteen and over. It assigns each entry a unique national identity number and provides for a chip card. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Morocco's law no. 72-18, on the targeting of beneficiaries of social support programmes, [was promulgated on 8 August 2020 and published in the Bulletin officiel on 7 January 2021](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/mor204689.pdf>). It creates the national population register and the national registers agency. Its second article [defines authentication as checking declared data online and in real time against the national population register](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/mor204689.pdf>). No bill to replace the law is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under it since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

Madagascar's law no. 2025-019 on the identification of natural persons was adopted by the National Assembly on 3 July 2025 and by the Senate on 4 July 2025. The President referred it for review before promulgation. On 26 August 2025 the High Constitutional Court [ruled that it conforms to the Constitution](<https://www.hcc.gov.mg/?p=9621>). That decision is the last step on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the law has been promulgated or that a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

Mali's law no. 06-040 of 11 August 2006 [institutes the national identification number and a national identification register](<https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2006/mali-jo-2006-28.pdf>). A decree of 18 October 2006 [fixes the fourteen-digit number and obliges public services to use it](<https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2006/mali-jo-2006-33.pdf>). A decree of 3 November 2022 [requires the number for any biometric identity card application](<https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2022/mali-jo-2022-35.pdf>) and cites the 2006 law as its basis. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

On 16 March 2022 the Assembly of the Republic [passed a bill in first reading](<https://www.parlamento.mz/?p=1695>) on civil identification and the identity card. In May 2025 the ICT regulator [listed Law 6/2022 on civil identification and the identity card](<https://www.id4africa.com/2025/files/PS5A-S1-4-Mozambique_FINAL.pdf>) among the laws in force. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 a [tender was launched for a consultancy on mobile digital identity and signatures](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-launches-tender-for-consultancy-on-mobile-digital-identity-and-signature-system/>). No source found says whether Law 6/2022 provides for a biometric register. None says whether it provides for a unique number or an electronic check. Operating would need a digital identity in the law in force.

Mauritania's identity system rests on its Civil Status Code, law no. 2011-003 of 12 January 2011. Law no. 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 [replaced three of its articles](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/117696/MRT-117696.pdf>). The code as amended [provides for the national biometric population register](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/117696/MRT-117696.pdf>) in its new article 31. Its new article 15 provides for digital civil status acts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Mauritius's identity card rests on the National Identity Card Act, No. 60 of 1985, which the identity card unit [lists as the law behind the card system](<https://mnis.govmu.org/>). The National Identity Card Regulations 2024 were [made by the minister on 16 February 2024](<https://paps.mnis.govmu.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/29_The-National-IC-Reg-2024-.pdf>) and revoke the regulations of 2013. Through them the Act [provides for a card that is biometric and can be checked electronically](<https://paps.mnis.govmu.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/29_The-National-IC-Reg-2024-.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is the issue of the new card from 19 February 2024.

Malawi's National Registration Act of 2010 [mandates the registration bureau to run the national registration and identification system](<https://mwnation.com/nrb-under-scrutiny/>), the Principal Secretary says. A 2025 presentation says [the National Registration Act No. 13 of 2010 was enacted as the legal foundation for the national digital identity system](<https://www.id4africa.com/2025/files/T3-P3-S2-3-Malawi_FINAL.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 23 July 2026 the Homeland Security Minister [made amendment regulations under it](<https://malawi24.com/2026/08/17/nrb-hikes-registration-fees/>), which [raised registration fees](<https://malawi24.com/2026/08/17/nrb-hikes-registration-fees/>). Fee changes do not count. No other rule made under the Act since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a regulation applying the Act, or a rule that others must check identity against it.

Namibia's Civil Registration and Identification Act, No. 13 of 2024, is [the statute for civil registration and legal identity](<https://namiblii.org/akn/na/act/2024/13/eng@2024-12-30>). The Act [assigns each person a unique identity number](<https://namiblii.org/akn/na/act/2024/13/eng@2024-12-30>) and authorises physical or electronic identity documents. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 an official of the Office of the Prime Minister said it [allows institutions to accept either the physical card or its digital version](<https://informante.web.na/?p=398234>). No change to the Act has been found. No regulation or decree made under it since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

On 22 April 2026 Niger's Council of Ministers [adopted a draft ordinance on the civil status regime](<https://www.gouv.ne/index.php/les-communiques-du-gouvernement/1143-conclusions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-22-avril-2026>). It amends law no. 2019-29 of 1 July 2019 and [would add biometric parameters and a unique identifier](<https://www.gouv.ne/index.php/les-communiques-du-gouvernement/1143-conclusions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-22-avril-2026>) to the registers that law set up. In the last twelve months this draft is the one change: until it is signed, the 2019 law stands as a civil status law. No source found says the draft has been signed, or that a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force.

Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 was [signed into law on 26 June 2026](<https://businessandtransport.com/how-nimc-emerges-nigerias-national-trust-authority-under-new-act-2026/>), repealing the 2007 Act. The Act [reaffirms the national identification number as the foundational identity and makes the Commission responsible for verifying electronic identities](<https://techcabal.com/2026/08/13/nigerias-identity-law-raises-questions-over-digital-signatures/>). It [makes the Commission the national repository for biometric data](<https://www.mondaq.com/nigeria/constitutional-administrative-law/1829270/the-national-identity-management-commission-establishment-act-2026-key-new-provisions>). On 29 July 2026 a civil society speaker said [the gazetted text was not yet available](<https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/08/nimc-act-2026-experts-demand-transparency-stronger-data-protection/>). In the last twelve months this Act replaced the 2007 Act. No regulation made under it has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

In March 2026 The New Times reported that Rwanda's law governing registration into its single digital identity system [sets a June 2027 deadline after which existing national identity cards are no longer valid](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/34398/news/technology/govt-sets-2027-deadline-for-full-shift-to-digital-id>). The system is [built on a unique digital identification number, a derived token and a card with a QR code](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/34398/news/technology/govt-sets-2027-deadline-for-full-shift-to-digital-id>). The identity agency's head said [the identity law was amended in 2023](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202406/legal-reforms-adapted-to-tech-changes-data-safeguards-vital-for-expanding-digital-id-reach>). The law's number and date are not given. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under it since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule.

Sudan's Civil Registry Act 2011 [was signed by the President, repealed the 2001 Act and came into force on signature](<https://citizenshiprightsafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/01/Sudan-Civil-Registration-Act-2011-EN.pdf>). The Act [defines the national number as a unique number given to each citizen on registration](<https://citizenshiprightsafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/01/Sudan-Civil-Registration-Act-2011-EN.pdf>). It provides for civil registry records to be stored electronically and for a central database. No later amendment is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Senegal's identity card rests on [a 2016 law instituting the ECOWAS biometric identity card](<https://senegaldirect.com/cartes-didentite-mouhamadou-moukhtar-cisse-explique-la-prorogation-exceptionnelle/>). In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a bill to amend it and extend how long cards are valid. On 29 September 2026 that bill, numbered 21/2026, [was before the National Assembly](<https://www.vipeoples.net/Passeports-et-cartes-d-identite-Vers-la-fin-du-contrat-avec-l-operateur-malaisien-et-le-recours-a-l-expertise-nationale_a184204.html>). An Interior Ministry official [said on 24 September 2026 that the amending text would extend the 2016 cards](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Societe/cartes-didentite-biometriques-de-2016-vers-une-prorogation-de-la-validite_n_505118.html>). No regulation or decree made under the 2016 law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need such a rule.

On 17 November 2025 Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority [held the final national validation of the draft National Civil Registration and Identification Bill](<https://thecalabashnewspaper.com/ncra-concludes-final-national-validation-of-draft-civil-registration-and-identification-bill/>) and its regulations. The bill has still to go to Cabinet and then to Parliament. It is the draft that would replace the present registration law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a law, ordinance or decree-law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

Somalia's Public Identification and Registration Law, Law No. 009 of 20 March 2023, is in force. On 8 June 2024 the Prime Minister [signed an implementing regulation made under it](<https://www.osagsomalia.com/media/documents/bulletins-contents/cabinet-decisions/2024/Xeer-nidaamiyaha_Sharciga_Aqoonsiga_Diiwaan-galinta_Dadwaynaha.pdf>), which took effect on signature. The regulation [applies the law and sets rules for relying parties](<https://www.osagsomalia.com/media/documents/bulletins-contents/cabinet-decisions/2024/Xeer-nidaamiyaha_Sharciga_Aqoonsiga_Diiwaan-galinta_Dadwaynaha.pdf>), among them banks and phone companies, which check identity against the system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is the regulation of 8 June 2024.

South Sudan's Civil Registry Act of 2018, with the Nationality Act of 2011, is [the legal foundation of its identification system](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>), a World Bank diagnostic of May 2026 says. The Civil Registration and National Identity Regulations, 2024, [were made under sections 33 and 39 of the Act](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>). The Bank says the two [lay the foundation for an interoperable digital identity system based on a personal identification number](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>). In the last twelve months the Act and regulations were cited and not changed. The Bank calls the framework under-implemented, and how far it is applied is the open question.

A World Bank mission of 8 to 12 September 2025 [flagged as urgent the review, public consultation, finalisation and approval](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102025185177863/pdf/P177158-d0ebd79d-6646-4e92-b9ae-1183b632c15a.pdf>) of São Tomé and Príncipe's new identity law. The mission's note calls it the aggregated identification document law and treats it as drafted and not yet approved. It [warned that without the law's approval the collection of data could be constrained](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102025185177863/pdf/P177158-d0ebd79d-6646-4e92-b9ae-1183b632c15a.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

Seychelles' National Identity Cards Act, Cap. 294, is in force. The Miscellaneous Amendments Act 2023, [assented to on 8 November 2023](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-11/Act%2022%20-%202023%20-%20Miscellaneous%20Amendments%20Act%202023.pdf>), amended it. The 2023 amendment [adds a card for non-resident citizens and new rules on disclosing card information](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-11/Act%2022%20-%202023%20-%20Miscellaneous%20Amendments%20Act%202023.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no replacement bill is on record. No source found says the law provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

Chad's Ordinance 002/PR/2020 of 14 February 2020 on civil status was [ratified by Law 006/PR/2020 of 29 May 2020](<https://www.refworld.org/sites/default/files/2026-05/tchad_etude_de_cas_inclusion_systeme_didentite_fr_avril_2026.pdf>). It sets up a system that issues a unique national identification number through the national biometric population register. In the last twelve months the ordinance was cited and not changed, in a UNHCR study of April 2026. In April 2025 the telecoms regulator ARCEP [said every SIM card sold must be linked to an NNI](<https://www.letchadanthropus-tribune.com/tchad-securite-larcep-sonnera-lalerte-sur-lappartenance-des-cartes-sim/>) under the texts in force. No source gives the rule or its date. Mature would need a regulation or decree applying the law, made in the past three years.

Togo's law no. 2020-009 of 10 September 2020 on the biometric identification of natural persons [created the national identification agency](<https://anid.gouv.tg/en/about-us/>). Law no. 2022-010 of 24 June 2022 amended several of its articles. The amended law [defines a unique identification number issued after verification of demographic and biometric data](<https://jo.gouv.tg/sites/default/files/JO/JOS_24_06_2022-67E%20ANNEE%20N%C2%B025%20BIS.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest rule found is a decree of 9 September 2022, and no rule made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

Tunisia's Organic Law No. 2024-22 of 11 March 2024 [amends and completes the 1993 law on the national identity card](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/loi-organique-n-2024-22-du-11-mars-2024-modifiant-et-completant-la-loi-n-93-27-du-22-mars-1993-relative-a-la-carte-nationale-didentite/>). It [provides that the identity card carries an encrypted electronic chip](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/loi-organique-n-2024-22-du-11-mars-2024-modifiant-et-completant-la-loi-n-93-27-du-22-mars-1993-relative-a-la-carte-nationale-didentite/>), which holds an electronic certificate for verifying identity and signing documents. In September 2025 La Presse reported that [the decrees on the card's model, specifications and security standards were still being prepared](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2025/09/21/tunisie-vers-le-lancement-imminent-de-la-carte-didentite-biometrique>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

Tanzania's Registration and Identification of Persons Act, first passed in 1986, [is recorded as still in force in the 2023 revised edition of the laws](<https://tanzanialaws.com/r/320-registration-and-identification-of-persons-act>). In the last twelve months, in January 2026 the government said it would [table an Infant Registration Bill in the session starting 27 January 2026](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202601/tanzania-working-on-legislative-framework-for-infant-id-registration>). The bill [would let the identification authority register children from birth](<https://dailynews.co.tz/nida-mulls-child-registration/>). No report says it has been tabled or passed. No source found says the 1986 Act provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

Uganda's Registration of Persons Act, 2015 [was assented to on 26 March 2015](<https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/2015/4/eng@2015-03-26>). The Act [has the Authority assign a unique national identification number to every person registered](<https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/2015/4/eng@2015-03-26>) and defines identity data to include fingerprints. Regulations [made under it on 12 August 2024](<https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/si/2024/67/eng@2024-08-12/source>) set the card's validity at eleven years. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A Parliament release of 20 August 2026 [describes the Authority as working under the Act](<https://www.parliament.go.ug/news/4571/new-id-system-faces-questions-over-digital-verification>), and in June 2026 the Authority said registered foreigners [are given a unique identification number under the Act](<https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/nira-kicks-off-first-registration-of-foreigne-NV_234932_062026>). The latest dated fact is the release of 20 August 2026.

South Africa's Identification Act of 1997 is in force. It [makes Home Affairs the sole authority keeping the National Population Register](<https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/government-amend-regulations-prevent-traffic-documents-being-used-identification>), and [its regulations were last amended on 23 June 2025](<https://www.dha.gov.za/images/gazettes/gazette-52893-230625-dha.pdf>). In the last twelve months, Home Affairs [gazetted draft regulations](<https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/smart-ids-go-digital-home-affairs-publishes-draft-rules/>) in May 2026 that [would regulate access to identity information](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202605/south-africa-gazettes-digital-id-draft-regulation-seeks-comments>); they were still drafts at the end of September 2026. A replacement bill [is due in Parliament only in 2027 or 2028](<https://techcentral.co.za/south-africa-behind-neighbours-digital-id/286057/>). No source found says the 1997 Act provides for a biometric register, a unique identity number or electronic checks. Operating would need a law in force that provides for digital identity.

Zambia's National Registration Regulations, 2019, Statutory Instrument No. 34 of 2019, [were made under section 14 of the National Registration Act](<https://www.zambialaws.com/Zambia2019Pdfsi/SI%2034%20of%202019.pdf>). The regulations [prescribe the registration procedure](<https://www.zambialaws.com/Zambia2019Pdfsi/SI%2034%20of%202019.pdf>), and require an application, a photograph, fingerprints and a birth certificate. No amendment to the Act since 2019 is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the Act provides for a biometric register. None says it provides for a unique number or electronic checks. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

Zimbabwe's National Registration Act [commenced on 24 September 1976](<https://zimlii.org/akn/zw/act/1976/36>). It provides for [the registration of residents and a register](<https://zimlii.org/akn/zw/act/1976/36>) kept by the Registrar-General. A statutory instrument [gazetted on 30 January 2024 was made under its section 11](<https://www.veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/SI%202024-010%20National%20Registration%20%28Fees%29%20%28Amendment%29%20Regulations%2C%202024%20%28No.%2018%29.pdf>) and amends the registration fees. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the Act, or an amendment to it, provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.
